facts.label: Source-by-source assessment
facts.text: - 20-F FY2025: filed annual report; controls audited year-end 2025 and 2024 facts. Issuer is the Luxembourg parent "MIC S.A." (chunk 91). Its debt note lists every bond by country and issuer (chunk 245-246) and every bank and DFI facility group (chunk 252). Total debt and financing is 6,886 at December 31, 2025 (chunk 245, chunk 110). The 20-F states "At December 31, 2025, there were no breaches of financial covenants and we do not anticipate any such breaches in the next twelve months" (chunk 258) but gives no covenant thresholds, ratios or headroom (chunk 116, chunk 258). - 6-K Q1: interim statements dated May 12, 2026 re-present 2025 comparatives for discontinued operations. Gross debt 8,624 and net debt 7,609 at March 31, 2026 appear in the release table (chunk 25 per the table row "Gross Debt 8,624 6,886 6,260 5,912 5,772"). Not reviewed by the auditor (no report in the file). - 6-K Q2: carries a KPMG Audit S.à r.l. review conclusion on the June 30, 2026 interim statements (chunk 8). Gross debt 8,742, net debt 8,075, leverage 2.73x (chunk 35-36). Prior-year income-statement columns are labeled "Not reviewed" (chunk 8). - 6-K Q3: latest period. Gross debt 8,648, cash 848, derivatives and vendor financing 183, net debt 7,983, leverage 2.53x at September 30, 2026 (chunk 32). Maturity ladder: one year 872, one to two years 986, two to three 1,947, three to four 1,601, four to five 1,147, after five 2,094, total 8,648 (chunk 25). Financial obligations note lists the quarter's issuances and repayments by country but not a facility-level balance table (chunks 23-25). No review report is in the file; statements are described as unaudited.

facts.label: Entity, perimeter and role map
facts.text: - Issuer and parent: Millicom International Cellular S.A. ("MIC S.A.", Luxembourg). Borrower of the corporate notes and the revolving credit facility. Guarantor of selected subsidiary facilities (parent guaranty for the Uruguay Santander loan, chunk 256-257; for the El Salvador IDB Invest loan, chunk 124; guarantees of $629 million at December 31, 2025, chunk 258). - Operating-level borrowers: Comunicaciones Celulares S.A. (Guatemala; $900 million 5.125% notes due 2032 issued through a trust with Guatemalan subsidiary guarantors, chunk 126), Telecomunicaciones Digitales, S.A. (Panama; 4.500% notes due 2030), Telefónica Celular del Paraguay S.A.E. (Paraguay; 5.875% notes due 2027, redeemed April 29, 2026 per chunk 25 of the Q3 6-K), UNE EPM Telecomunicaciones (Colombia bonds), Colombia Telecomunicaciones S.A. E.S.P. ("Coltel", acquired February 6, 2026; Q3 6-K chunk 9), and others. At December 31, 2025, 65 percent ($4,470 million) of debt was at operating level and generally non-recourse to MIC S.A. (chunk 114); the Q3 release states roughly 70 percent operating-entity and 30 percent corporate (chunk 32). - Equity-accounted entities, not consolidated: Honduras joint venture (MIC S.A. holds 66.67 percent but joint control applies, chunk 92) and the Chile associate (49 percent through Celtel Chile, S.L., Q3 6-K chunk 11). Segment tables present both at 100 percent and eliminate them to reach group totals (Q3 6-K chunk 17). - No restricted or unrestricted group definitions, guarantor groups or obligor perimeters for covenant tests are supplied; indentures are listed as exhibits in the 20-F (chunks 125-127) but are not in the source set.

facts.label: Period and basis relationships (versions kept separate)
facts.text: - The 20-F balance sheet at December 31, 2025 is the original audited version. The Q3 6-K restates the December 31, 2025 comparatives for final Uruguay and updated Ecuador purchase accounting (chunk 4 footnote and chunk 12 table). Both versions stay active; the 20-F controls the audited figure and the Q3 6-K controls the restated comparative. - 2025 income-statement comparatives in all three 6-Ks are re-presented to move Tigo Paraguay's mobile finance business to discontinued operations (Q3 6-K chunks 1, 12, 15); the 20-F FY2025 statements are not re-presented. Cash flow and balance sheet items are not re-presented (Q3 6-K chunk 41 footnote 5). - Quarter versus year-to-date: the Q3 income statement gives both three-month and nine-month columns (chunk 1). The earnings release gives Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026, Q2 2026, Q1 2026, Q4 2025 and Q3 2025 (chunk 41), which supports discrete quarters. The Q4 2025 discrete cash flow, capex and tax are not given as a quarter in the 6-Ks. - Perimeter: Coltel is consolidated from February 6, 2026, Tigo Uruguay and Tigo Ecuador from October 2025 (Q3 6-K chunks 1-2), so year-on-year growth is largely inorganic (the release gives organic growth of 4.8 percent revenue and 7.7 percent Adjusted EBITDA for Q3, chunk 41). Pro forma Coltel for 9M is stated only as incremental revenue $132 million and incremental net loss $34 million (chunk 10). - Non-IFRS: Adjusted EBITDA, net debt, leverage, capex, OCF and equity free cash flow are management measures defined in the release (chunk 40) and reconciled in part (chunks 41-43). The statement definition of Adjusted EBITDA (note 5 footnote ii, chunk 18) and the release definition (chunk 40) are worded differently, and the leverage ratio is net debt over LTM Adjusted EBITDA after lease depreciation and lease interest, pro forma for acquisitions (chunk 40), so it is not a covenant ratio. - Management claims (for example the guidance of equity free cash flow around $1.1 billion and year-end leverage below 2.5x, chunk 29) are attributed supporting claims and do not override the statements.

facts.label: Interpretation (evidence, risk mechanism, credit implication)
facts.text: - Leverage. Evidence: net debt rose from 5,357 at December 31, 2025 to 7,983 at September 30, 2026 while management leverage moved from 2.17x to 2.53x, after a peak of 2.76x at March 31, 2026 (release tables). Mechanism: the debt increase came mainly from consolidating Coltel and paying for the Colombian stakes, offset by a larger EBITDA base and strong cash generation; the ratio is pro forma and net of lease costs. Implication: leverage has improved for two consecutive quarters, but the reported figure rests on a management denominator that is not reproducible from the supplied tables (Calculations 3 and 4), and covenant headroom cannot be assessed because covenant terms are not supplied. - Coverage. Evidence: interest expense on bonds and bank financing was 472 for nine months against Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958, with lease interest of 232 on top. Mechanism: the average cost of debt was 8.3 percent and 44 percent of debt is floating (the fixed-rate share is 56 percent), so rate moves pass through to interest; local-currency borrowing of 61 percent of debt matches revenue currencies but carries higher coupons than the dollar book (5.7 percent on dollar debt). Implication: coverage is adequate on the reported period (Calculation 6) but the Coltel floating-rate debt raises sensitivity to rates; interest sensitivity is Not supplied. - Cash flow quality. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958 converts to operating cash flow of 2,289 after capex and to equity free cash flow of 867 after spectrum, taxes, interest and lease payments; 9M dividends paid of 587 consumed most of it. Mechanism: lease payments (483 net for nine months) and spectrum (207) are large fixed claims; restructuring items above EBITDA of 149 depress EBITDA temporarily. Implication: free cash flow after dividends was about 280 for the nine months (Calculation 8) while acquisitions required 924, so the group funded the Colombian deals with cash, debt and equity buy-outs of minorities rather than with internally generated cash alone. - Liquidity. Evidence: cash of 848 against debt due within one year of 872, and a 600 revolving facility that was undrawn at December 31, 2025 and due October 2027. Mechanism: the near-term ladder is dominated by operating-level bank loans that are routinely rolled (the Q3 notes show repeated refinancing), and the 2027 SEK note and revolving facility mature within about fourteen months. Implication: liquidity depends on continued market access and on facility availability that the 6-Ks do not confirm; the current-year dividend schedule adds a visible cash call (Calculation 7). - Data quality. Evidence: Q1 and Q3 are unreviewed; the December 31, 2025 balance sheet was restated; purchase accounting for Coltel is provisional; the cash flow statement and the release disagree on 9M operating cash flow (2,028 against 2,019). Implication: figures are usable as reported with labels, but any single-period ratio mixing restated and original bases carries an unresolved difference. - Definition risks. Evidence: management leverage and Adjusted EBITDA are non-IFRS and defined differently across the segment note and the release. Implication: do not equate the release leverage with a covenant ratio; do not compare it with ratios built from IFRS lines without stating the bridge.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Colombia consolidation. On January 27, 2026 Millicom was awarded 100 percent of EPM's remaining shares in UNE EPM Telecomunicaciones S.A. at a price of COP 418,741 per share, about COP 2.1 trillion (about $571 million); the deal closed January 29, 2026 and was accounted for as an equity transaction that reduced equity by $627 million (Q3 6-K chunk 8). On February 6, 2026 it closed the purchase of Telefónica's controlling 67.5 percent of Colombia Telecomunicaciones S.A. E.S.P. (Coltel) for about $214.4 million, of which $169 million was paid at acquisition (Q3 6-K chunk 9). Coltel was acquired with "Other debt and financing" of $1,424 million and lease liabilities of $515 million at fair value, and contributed revenue of $1,127 million and a net loss of $168 million from acquisition to September 30, 2026, including about $71 million of severance (Q3 6-K chunks 9-10). On April 27, 2026 it bought the remaining 32.5 percent from La Nación, a $219 million equity transaction (Q3 6-K chunk 9). The purchase accounting remains provisional. Creditor mechanic: control of the combined Colombian business is now full, which removes minority leakage and approvals but added acquired debt and integration costs; the management leverage rose to 2.76x at March 31, 2026 before falling to 2.53x at September 30, 2026 (CP-1). The Colombian joint operations (UNIRED and UT) are consolidated in full from the Coltel acquisition, and EPM remains a non-controlling partner in certain operations (Q3 6-K chunks 5, 22).

facts.text: Ecuador and Uruguay. Millicom completed the purchase of Telefónica Móviles del Uruguay on October 7, 2025 for an enterprise value of $440 million and of Telefónica's Ecuador operations on October 30, 2025 for an enterprise value of $380 million (Q3 6-K chunks 13-14). Uruguay accounting is final; Ecuador's measurement period ended October 30, 2026 and was still being finalized when the statements were issued. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Chile with NJJ. On February 10, 2026 Celtel Chile, S.L. (49 percent Millicom, 51 percent NJJ Cactus SAS) bought Telefónica Móviles Chile for $50 million cash with contingent earn-outs "without recourse to Millicom"; Celtel carries a recognized liability of $110 million at September 30, 2026, funded by external financial debt, and mutual call options exist from the fifth and sixth anniversaries (Q3 6-K chunk 11). It is equity-accounted and the carrying value is nil because losses exceeded the investment, leaving $41 million of unrecognized losses at Millicom's share (Q3 6-K chunk 22). The 20-F describes the earn-out as up to $150 million (20-F chunk 297) and the 6-Ks as up to $490 million (see Conflicts). NJJ is described in the related party note as part of Xavier Niel's holdings (20-F chunk 295), so this is a joint investment with a party linked to the controlling shareholder; terms are as disclosed and the pricing basis of the options is not quantified.

facts.text: Tower monetization and leaseback. On October 28, 2024 Millicom agreed to sell Lati International and other assets, more than 7,000 towers in Central America, to SBA Communications Corp. with a 15-year leaseback and a build-to-suit commitment for up to 2,500 further sites; Lati Paraguay was sold to Atis Group on June 3, 2025; the gain recognized in 2025 was $741 million (Q3 6-K chunks 14-15). Millicom retains Lati subsidiaries in Bolivia with about 2,000 towers (20-F chunk 91). Creditor mechanic (Analyst Interpretation): the sale converted owned assets into leased ones, so the leaseback added lease liabilities that rank as fixed claims; how the proceeds were applied is not stated in the sources reviewed.

facts.text: New debt issues and refinancings in 2026 (all subsequent to the 20-F balance sheet date). MIC S.A. reopened its 7.375% Senior Notes due 2032 for an additional $87.5 million in a Regulation S private placement on April 14, 2026, admitted to the Euro MTF market, placed with Banco General, S.A.; MIC S.A. issued an 8-year COP-USD linked private bond for COP 370,000 million at a fixed rate on March 27, 2026, subscribed by the Inter-American Development Bank and Proparco (Q3 6-K chunk 24). Tigo Paraguay redeemed its 5.875% notes due 2027, about $139.7 million, at par on April 29, 2026 (Q3 6-K chunk 25). Coltel entered a one-year $100 million bridge facility with Banco Santander at variable rate on April 13, 2026 to repay a $100 million HSBC facility, and later new three-year and one-year variable bank loans in Colombian pesos; Tigo Colombia added a four-year variable loan with Davivienda of COP 220,000 million; Tigo Panama refinanced a $75 million loan with a new six-year BAC loan in August 2026; Tigo Guatemala, Tigo Bolivia and others added bank loans (Q3 6-K chunks 23-25). After the quarter, Coltel took a COP 40,000 million BTG Pactual loan and prepaid $12.5 million of the Santander loan on October 15, 2026 (Q3 6-K chunk 28, subsequent event). Instrument-level terms such as ranking, security, covenants and guarantor groups are Not supplied for these issues, and use of proceeds is stated only for the Coltel bridge. Gross debt rose from $6,886 million to $8,648 million over the nine months (CP-1).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: service revenue of 6,045 for nine months 2026 against 3,888, with organic service revenue growth of 5.3 percent (Q3 6-K chunk 41), most of the growth coming from consolidating Coltel, Ecuador and Uruguay. Mechanism: recurring subscription revenue across twelve countries gives scale, and prepaid-to-postpaid migration raises visibility, but the acquired revenue base has a short history under Millicom control and the underlying organic rate is mid-single-digit. Implication: revenue is large and recurring; the comparison to prior years is flattered by perimeter, so organic growth is the better guide to durability. Conflict that counters it: none logged. 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 45.9 percent for nine months 2026 against 47.3 percent, with 149 of one-off items above Adjusted EBITDA (Q3 6-K chunks 34, 41). Mechanism: Coltel integration and restructuring are depressing near-term margin and consuming cash, while lease payments and spectrum are fixed claims. Implication: coverage and free cash flow depend on delivering the Colombian cost program; if integration slips, equity free cash flow guidance is at risk (management claim). Conflict that counters it: C3 does not change cash flow; the unreconciled operating cash flow figures in CP-1 gap G5 limit precision. 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: Guatemala and the two Colombian segments carry the largest segment revenue and the Guatemala entity issues $900 million 5.125% notes with subsidiary guarantees. Mechanism: a regulatory, currency or macro event in one of these countries affects a large share of consolidated EBITDA and the operating-level debt serviced from it. Implication: monitor country-level cash availability and the share of debt at operating entities (about 70 percent, Q3 6-K chunk 32), noting that MIC S.A. is dependent on upstream dividends (20-F chunk 111). 4. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: controlling shareholder holds about 42.2 percent, appoints four of eight non-executive directors, and has a related-party payable and a joint investment. Mechanism: aligned equity ownership can support the issuer, but larger distributions (a $1.50 interim on top of the regular dividend) and a related investment competing for cash with creditors are potential leakage channels. Implication: neutral to mixed on documented actions; the absence of documented creditor-adverse actions is not evidence that covenants prevent them because indentures are not supplied. Conflict that counters it: C2. 5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: Coltel and Ecuador purchase accounting provisional; covenant terms, debt schedule and revolving facility status not supplied; Chile earn-out size in conflict (C1); Guatemala litigation settled but other claims remain. Mechanism: each limits the ability to size liquidity and covenant headroom. Implication: committee readiness is limited until the named documents are obtained.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Rationale (evidence, mechanism, implication): Millicom is a large, scaled, recurring-revenue operator across twelve Latin American countries whose earnings base has stepped up sharply through the 2025 and 2026 acquisitions in Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay. The consolidated net debt increased from 5,357 at December 31, 2025 to 7,983 at September 30, 2026, and management leverage moved from 2.17x to a peak of 2.76x and then to 2.53x at September 30, 2026. The mechanism is that purchase payments, consolidated acquired debt and a heavier lease and dividend burden were absorbed by a much larger EBITDA and equity free cash flow base; deleveraging now depends on integrating Colombia and delivering the stated cash flow. The credit implication is a business with sound operating scale and improving cash generation but with high absolute leverage, material lease obligations outside the headline measure, a near-term maturity and refinancing agenda and an incomplete view of covenant headroom. The fundamental view is therefore that debt service capacity appears supported on the reported period, with the quality of that support limited by perimeter effects, definition risk and missing legal documents. The confidence is Medium rather than High because covenant terms, instrument-level debt after December 31, 2025, the revolving facility position and indentures are not in the evidence set.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. The credit story is a consolidation story. Nine-month 2026 revenue of 6,440 and Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958 compare with 4,150 and 1,964 a year earlier, but the release attributes most of the growth to perimeter and currency, with organic revenue growth of 4.4 percent and organic Adjusted EBITDA growth of 8.8 percent. Basis: CP-1 figures and the CP-1A volume-drivers and Colombia transaction rows. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures; the reading that organic growth is the better durability guide is Analyst Interpretation. Mechanism: acquired revenue lifts coverage but has a short record under Millicom control. Implication: durability should be judged on organic trends and on the Colombian integration outcome. 2. Leverage has improved for two consecutive quarters but is measured on a management basis that cannot be reproduced. Management leverage fell from 2.76x at March 31, 2026 to 2.73x and then 2.53x at September 30, 2026, against a year-end target of below 2.5x. Simple net debt over reported last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 2.14x and 2.99x when lease liabilities are added (CP-1 Calculation 3). Category: Documentary Fact for the reported ratio and Analyst Interpretation for the simple ratios. Mechanism: lease costs are subtracted in the management denominator and acquisitions are pro forma, neither bridge is supplied. Implication: use the lease-inclusive view alongside the headline ratio, and treat the 2.5x target as a management claim. 3. Debt service capacity is supported by cash generation but nearly all of it is claimed by fixed uses. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958 covers interest on bonds and bank financing of 472 about 6.3 times and covers that plus lease interest about 4.2 times (CP-1 Calculation 6); equity free cash flow of 867 was followed by dividends paid of 587, leaving about 280 against acquisition payments of 924. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation. Mechanism: lease payments, spectrum and taxes are the largest fixed claims ahead of equity free cash flow. Implication: cushion for unplanned shocks is thinner than the headline EBITDA suggests. 4. Liquidity relies on refinancing access. Cash of 848 equals debt due within one year of 872; the 2027 SEK note and the 600 revolving facility, which was undrawn at December 31, 2025 and due October 2027, mature within about fourteen months, and the facility's current availability is Not supplied. Category: Documentary Fact for balances and maturities, Insufficient Information for facility availability. Mechanism: local bank facilities have been rolled routinely in 2026 and bond market access was shown by the 2032 notes reopening, but a dislocation would hit the near-term ladder first. Implication: monitor facility status and the 2027 maturities. 5. Shareholder distributions are rising at the same time as leverage is being reduced. The Board approved an interim dividend of $1.50 per share in August 2026 on top of the regular $3.00 per share cycle; the controlling shareholder group holds about 42.2 percent of voting shares. Scheduled cash dividends of about 629 follow September 30, 2026 (CP-1 Calculation 7). Category: Documentary Fact for the declared amounts; Analyst Interpretation for the pressure on deleveraging. Mechanism: distributions compete with debt reduction for equity free cash flow. Implication: neutral to mixed behaviour on the evidence, because capacity limits in the debt documents are not supplied. 6. Control and related-party links are concentrated. One shareholder group holds de facto control and four of eight non-executive board seats; a payable to the Iliad Holding Group of 195 at December 31, 2025 has no stated nature, and the Chile investment is held with NJJ, a party linked to the controlling shareholder. Category: Documentary Fact; absence of documented creditor-adverse actions is not evidence of contractual protection. Implication: governance risk is moderated by alignment but cannot be sized without the indentures. 7. Data quality and definition risk limit precision. The December 31, 2025 balance sheet was restated, 2025 comparatives were re-presented, Coltel and Ecuador purchase accounting is provisional, Q1 and Q3 statements are unreviewed, the Chile earn-out is stated as up to $150 million in the 20-F and up to $490 million in the 6-Ks (conflict C1), and 9M operating cash flow differs by 9 between the cash flow statement and the release reconciliation. Category: Documentary Fact. Implication: carry both values and label bases; do not treat any single reconciled figure as settled.

facts.text: Strengths. - Scale and diversification. Category: Documentary Fact. citations.quote: Weaknesses.

- High absolute leverage and lease burden. Category: Documentary Fact. Net debt of 7,983 and lease liabilities of 3,190; lease-inclusive net financing obligations of 11,173 against reported last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 3,734 (Analyst Interpretation on the ratio). Mechanism: leases rank as fixed charges and the tower leaseback increased them.

- Emerging-market, correlated exposure and currency volatility. Category: Documentary Fact. The release cites rapid appreciation of the Colombian peso, Paraguayan guarani and Boliviano and a regime change in Bolivia. Mechanism: reported dollar results and local-currency debt values swing with exchange rates; reversal would reduce dollar EBITDA.

- Integration and execution risk in Colombia. Category: Documentary Fact for the restructuring charges and the Coltel net loss; Analyst Interpretation for the risk. Mechanism: severance and integration costs reduce EBITDA and cash flow and delay synergies.

- Floating-rate exposure and cost of debt. Category: Documentary Fact. Fixed-rate debt fell to 56 percent of debt and the average interest rate was 8.3 percent. Mechanism: higher rates pass through to interest expense; rate sensitivity is Not supplied (Insufficient Information).
- Near-term maturities and facility dependence. Category: Documentary Fact. Cash of 848 against debt due within one year of 872. Mechanism: refinancing needs are recurring.
- Controlling shareholder influence and distributions. Category: Documentary Fact. See key finding 5 and 6.

- Provisional accounting and limited legal visibility. Category: Insufficient Information. Covenant definitions, indentures, guarantor groups and the revolving facility position are not in the evidence set, so legal capacity for distributions, asset transfers and priming cannot be assessed.

## Findings
### Source-set summary

The set is one audited annual report (20-F for FY2025) and three furnished 6-K packages (Q1, H1 and 9M 2026), each combining IFRS interim statements with an earnings release. No presentation deck, indenture, credit agreement, rating report, covenant compliance certificate or workbook is supplied. The latest source (6-K dated November 5, 2026) is dated on the as-of date; nothing later is used.

Evidence to risk mechanism to consequence: the filed statements give consolidated debt, cash, leverage, cash flow and quarterly Adjusted EBITDA for five quarter-ends, so CP-1 can build period tables. The perimeter changed sharply in 2026, so every period comparison needs the perimeter caveats below. Facility-level and covenant terms stop at December 31, 2025, so any statement about current covenant headroom cannot be sourced and must stay a gap.
### Source-by-source assessment

- 20-F FY2025: filed annual report; controls audited year-end 2025 and 2024 facts. Issuer is the Luxembourg parent "MIC S.A." (chunk 91). Its debt note lists every bond by country and issuer (chunk 245-246) and every bank and DFI facility group (chunk 252). Total debt and financing is 6,886 at December 31, 2025 (chunk 245, chunk 110). The 20-F states "At December 31, 2025, there were no breaches of financial covenants and we do not anticipate any such breaches in the next twelve months" (chunk 258) but gives no covenant thresholds, ratios or headroom (chunk 116, chunk 258).

- 6-K Q1: interim statements dated May 12, 2026 re-present 2025 comparatives for discontinued operations. Gross debt 8,624 and net debt 7,609 at March 31, 2026 appear in the release table (chunk 25 per the table row "Gross Debt 8,624 6,886 6,260 5,912 5,772"). Not reviewed by the auditor (no report in the file).

- 6-K Q2: carries a KPMG Audit S.à r.l. review conclusion on the June 30, 2026 interim statements (chunk 8). Gross debt 8,742, net debt 8,075, leverage 2.73x (chunk 35-36). Prior-year income-statement columns are labeled "Not reviewed" (chunk 8).

- 6-K Q3: latest period. Gross debt 8,648, cash 848, derivatives and vendor financing 183, net debt 7,983, leverage 2.53x at September 30, 2026 (chunk 32). Maturity ladder: one year 872, one to two years 986, two to three 1,947, three to four 1,601, four to five 1,147, after five 2,094, total 8,648 (chunk 25). Financial obligations note lists the quarter's issuances and repayments by country but not a facility-level balance table (chunks 23-25). No review report is in the file; statements are described as unaudited.
### Entity, perimeter and role map

- Issuer and parent: Millicom International Cellular S.A. ("MIC S.A.", Luxembourg). Borrower of the corporate notes and the revolving credit facility. Guarantor of selected subsidiary facilities (parent guaranty for the Uruguay Santander loan, chunk 256-257; for the El Salvador IDB Invest loan, chunk 124; guarantees of $629 million at December 31, 2025, chunk 258).

- Operating-level borrowers: Comunicaciones Celulares S.A. (Guatemala; $900 million 5.125% notes due 2032 issued through a trust with Guatemalan subsidiary guarantors, chunk 126), Telecomunicaciones Digitales, S.A. (Panama; 4.500% notes due 2030), Telefónica Celular del Paraguay S.A.E. (Paraguay; 5.875% notes due 2027, redeemed April 29, 2026 per chunk 25 of the Q3 6-K), UNE EPM Telecomunicaciones (Colombia bonds), Colombia Telecomunicaciones S.A. E.S.P. ("Coltel", acquired February 6, 2026; Q3 6-K chunk 9), and others. At December 31, 2025, 65 percent ($4,470 million) of debt was at operating level and generally non-recourse to MIC S.A. (chunk 114); the Q3 release states roughly 70 percent operating-entity and 30 percent corporate (chunk 32).

- Equity-accounted entities, not consolidated: Honduras joint venture (MIC S.A. holds 66.67 percent but joint control applies, chunk 92) and the Chile associate (49 percent through Celtel Chile, S.L., Q3 6-K chunk 11). Segment tables present both at 100 percent and eliminate them to reach group totals (Q3 6-K chunk 17).

- No restricted or unrestricted group definitions, guarantor groups or obligor perimeters for covenant tests are supplied; indentures are listed as exhibits in the 20-F (chunks 125-127) but are not in the source set.
### Period and basis relationships (versions kept separate)

- The 20-F balance sheet at December 31, 2025 is the original audited version. The Q3 6-K restates the December 31, 2025 comparatives for final Uruguay and updated Ecuador purchase accounting (chunk 4 footnote and chunk 12 table). Both versions stay active; the 20-F controls the audited figure and the Q3 6-K controls the restated comparative.

- 2025 income-statement comparatives in all three 6-Ks are re-presented to move Tigo Paraguay's mobile finance business to discontinued operations (Q3 6-K chunks 1, 12, 15); the 20-F FY2025 statements are not re-presented. Cash flow and balance sheet items are not re-presented (Q3 6-K chunk 41 footnote 5).

- Quarter versus year-to-date: the Q3 income statement gives both three-month and nine-month columns (chunk 1). The earnings release gives Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2026, Q2 2026, Q1 2026, Q4 2025 and Q3 2025 (chunk 41), which supports discrete quarters. The Q4 2025 discrete cash flow, capex and tax are not given as a quarter in the 6-Ks.

- Perimeter: Coltel is consolidated from February 6, 2026, Tigo Uruguay and Tigo Ecuador from October 2025 (Q3 6-K chunks 1-2), so year-on-year growth is largely inorganic (the release gives organic growth of 4.8 percent revenue and 7.7 percent Adjusted EBITDA for Q3, chunk 41). Pro forma Coltel for 9M is stated only as incremental revenue $132 million and incremental net loss $34 million (chunk 10).

- Non-IFRS: Adjusted EBITDA, net debt, leverage, capex, OCF and equity free cash flow are management measures defined in the release (chunk 40) and reconciled in part (chunks 41-43). The statement definition of Adjusted EBITDA (note 5 footnote ii, chunk 18) and the release definition (chunk 40) are worded differently, and the leverage ratio is net debt over LTM Adjusted EBITDA after lease depreciation and lease interest, pro forma for acquisitions (chunk 40), so it is not a covenant ratio.

- Management claims (for example the guidance of equity free cash flow around $1.1 billion and year-end leverage below 2.5x, chunk 29) are attributed supporting claims and do not override the statements.

### Interpretation (evidence, risk mechanism, credit implication)

- Leverage. Evidence: net debt rose from 5,357 at December 31, 2025 to 7,983 at September 30, 2026 while management leverage moved from 2.17x to 2.53x, after a peak of 2.76x at March 31, 2026 (release tables). Mechanism: the debt increase came mainly from consolidating Coltel and paying for the Colombian stakes, offset by a larger EBITDA base and strong cash generation; the ratio is pro forma and net of lease costs. Implication: leverage has improved for two consecutive quarters, but the reported figure rests on a management denominator that is not reproducible from the supplied tables (Calculations 3 and 4), and covenant headroom cannot be assessed because covenant terms are not supplied.

- Coverage. Evidence: interest expense on bonds and bank financing was 472 for nine months against Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958, with lease interest of 232 on top. Mechanism: the average cost of debt was 8.3 percent and 44 percent of debt is floating (the fixed-rate share is 56 percent), so rate moves pass through to interest; local-currency borrowing of 61 percent of debt matches revenue currencies but carries higher coupons than the dollar book (5.7 percent on dollar debt). Implication: coverage is adequate on the reported period (Calculation 6) but the Coltel floating-rate debt raises sensitivity to rates; interest sensitivity is Not supplied.

- Cash flow quality. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958 converts to operating cash flow of 2,289 after capex and to equity free cash flow of 867 after spectrum, taxes, interest and lease payments; 9M dividends paid of 587 consumed most of it. Mechanism: lease payments (483 net for nine months) and spectrum (207) are large fixed claims; restructuring items above EBITDA of 149 depress EBITDA temporarily. Implication: free cash flow after dividends was about 280 for the nine months (Calculation 8) while acquisitions required 924, so the group funded the Colombian deals with cash, debt and equity buy-outs of minorities rather than with internally generated cash alone.

- Liquidity. Evidence: cash of 848 against debt due within one year of 872, and a 600 revolving facility that was undrawn at December 31, 2025 and due October 2027. Mechanism: the near-term ladder is dominated by operating-level bank loans that are routinely rolled (the Q3 notes show repeated refinancing), and the 2027 SEK note and revolving facility mature within about fourteen months. Implication: liquidity depends on continued market access and on facility availability that the 6-Ks do not confirm; the current-year dividend schedule adds a visible cash call (Calculation 7).

- Data quality. Evidence: Q1 and Q3 are unreviewed; the December 31, 2025 balance sheet was restated; purchase accounting for Coltel is provisional; the cash flow statement and the release disagree on 9M operating cash flow (2,028 against 2,019). Implication: figures are usable as reported with labels, but any single-period ratio mixing restated and original bases carries an unresolved difference.

- Definition risks. Evidence: management leverage and Adjusted EBITDA are non-IFRS and defined differently across the segment note and the release. Implication: do not equate the release leverage with a covenant ratio; do not compare it with ratios built from IFRS lines without stating the bridge.
## Calculations
All inputs are quoted from the sources above; results are calculated by this module, not printed by the issuer. Rounding is to the stated precision.
### Calculation 1: Discrete quarter cash flow from cumulative statements

- Q2 2026 operating cash flow = H1 2026 1,301 minus Q1 2026 590 = 711. Q3 2026 = 9M 2,028 minus H1 1,301 = 727, which equals the Q3 figure printed in the equity free cash flow reconciliation (727, Q3 6-K chunk 42), so the cash flow statement ties at quarter level.
- Q2 2026 cash interest paid on debt = H1 279 minus Q1 138 = 141; Q3 = 9M 463 minus H1 279 = 184.
### Calculation 2: Last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA as printed, not pro forma

- LTM to September 30, 2026 = Q4 2025 776 + Q1 2026 857 + Q2 2026 1,009 + Q3 2026 1,092 = 3,734 (quarterly series in Q3 6-K chunk 41). Basis limitation: Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 include only part of the Coltel, Uruguay and Ecuador contribution, so this is not a pro forma figure.

- Cross-check: the FY2025 20-F figure of 2,749 less re-presented 9M 2025 of 1,964 plus 9M 2026 of 2,958 would be 3,743; the nine-unit difference arises because the 20-F figure is not re-presented for discontinued operations.
### Calculation 3: Simple leverage ratios (calculated, unadjusted for pro forma or leases)
- Net debt 7,983 divided by LTM Adjusted EBITDA 3,734 = 2.14x.
- Gross debt 8,648 divided by 3,734 = 2.32x.
- Lease-inclusive: net debt 7,983 plus lease liabilities 3,190 (2,846 non-current plus 344 current) = 11,173; divided by 3,734 = 2.99x.

- Management leverage is 2.53x. Dividing net debt 7,983 by 2.53 implies a denominator of about 3,155, which is lower than 3,734 by about 579; management subtracts depreciation of right-of-use assets and lease interest and adds pro forma acquisition EBITDA, and neither the right-of-use depreciation by quarter nor the pro forma bridge is supplied. The management ratio is therefore Not calculable from the supplied tables.
### Calculation 4: Net debt and gross debt movements

- Gross debt 8,648 minus 6,886 at December 31, 2025 = 1,762. Net debt 7,983 minus 5,357 = 2,626. The Q1 release attributes 1,482 of the gross debt increase and 1,513 of the net debt increase in Q1 to consolidating Coltel and 773 of Q1 net debt to acquisition-related payments (Q1 6-K chunk 24); the remaining components are not summed here.

- Gearing as defined in the 20-F (net debt divided by equity attributable to owners plus net debt): December 31, 2025 = 5,357 / (3,640 + 5,357) = 0.60 (printed 0.60 in 20-F chunk 273); September 30, 2026 = 7,983 / (2,238 + 7,983) = 0.78.
### Calculation 5: Maturity concentration at September 30, 2026
- Due within one year 872 / 8,648 = 10.1 percent; within two years (872 + 986) = 1,858 / 8,648 = 21.5 percent; after five years 2,094 / 8,648 = 24.2 percent.
- Cash 848 / debt due within one year 872 = 0.97x.
### Calculation 6: Interest coverage, nine months to September 30, 2026
- Adjusted EBITDA 2,958 / interest expense on bonds and bank financing 472 = 6.27x.
- Adjusted EBITDA 2,958 / (472 + lease interest 232) = 4.20x.
- Adjusted EBITDA 2,958 / cash interest paid (463 on debt plus 216 on leases) = 4.36x.

- Basis: interest expense and Adjusted EBITDA both include Coltel from February 6, 2026 and Uruguay and Ecuador from October 2025, so the ratios are on a reported basis and not pro forma. The 44 percent floating share used in the interpretation is 100 percent minus the printed 56 percent fixed share.
### Calculation 7: Scheduled dividend cash calls after September 30, 2026

- Remaining declared installments: October 2026 0.75; January 2027 0.75 plus 0.75; April 2027 0.75 plus 0.75 = 3.75 per share. Multiply by 167.717 million weighted average shares for Q3 2026 (Q3 6-K chunk 20) = about 629. The balance sheet dividend payable is 579; the difference of about 50 is not explained in the sources (possibly the October installment timing or share count), so 629 is an approximation.
### Calculation 8: Cash generation and uses, nine months to September 30, 2026
- Equity free cash flow 867 minus dividends paid 587 = 280.
- Operating cash flow (Adjusted EBITDA less capex) 2,289 / Adjusted EBITDA 2,958 = 77.4 percent.

- Adjusted EBITDA excluding the 149 one-offs reported above EBITDA = 2,958 + 149 = 3,107; for Q3, 1,092 + 31 = 1,123. This adds back the issuer's own one-off classification; the one-offs are not independently verified.
- Implied fourth-quarter equity free cash flow if the around-1.1-billion guidance were met exactly = 1,100 minus 867 = 233 (management claim, approximate).

- LTM equity free cash flow excluding divestitures = FY2025 864 minus 9M 2025 601 plus 9M 2026 867 = 1,130; net debt 7,983 / 1,130 = 7.1x. Basis mix: FY2025 is not re-presented while 9M 2025 is, and the perimeter changed, so this ratio is indicative only.
### Calculation 9: FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA margin
- 2,749 / 5,819 = 47.2 percent (the 20-F does not print a margin).

Subject: Millicom International Cellular S.A. (issuer id tigo; "MIC S.A.", the Luxembourg parent of the Tigo group). As-of date: 2026-11-05 (cutoff 2026-11-05). Module: CP-1A, business and transaction context, pathway credit_snapshot, public case, creditor perspective.

Reader question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor of the group? Decision drivers: transaction and ownership structure; business and operating model; credit-relevant history or change. This module gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion. Company claims about market position are the issuer's own and are labelled as such.

Fact categories used on every fact row: Documentary Fact (the cited source states it); Management Language (management's characterisation, quoted and not adopted); Analyst Interpretation (this module's reading of cited evidence); Insufficient Information (evidence missing; the missing datapoint and why it matters are stated). Locator convention: "chunk N" is the `page` field of the named converted-text file. Source labels: 20-F = 20-F_2025-12-31_tigo-20251231.htm.jsonl; Q1 6-K = 6-K_2026-05-12_dp246578_6k.htm.jsonl; Q2 6-K = 6-K_2026-08-06_dp251442_6k.htm.jsonl; Q3 6-K = 6-K_2026-11-05_dp256407_6k.htm.jsonl. ### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The set contains no single leveraged-finance transaction; the creditor-relevant transactions are the 2025 and 2026 acquisitions, the asset monetization and the 2026 financings. Each item is a Documentary Fact from the filings unless it says otherwise.

Colombia consolidation. On January 27, 2026 Millicom was awarded 100 percent of EPM's remaining shares in UNE EPM Telecomunicaciones S.A. at a price of COP 418,741 per share, about COP 2.1 trillion (about $571 million); the deal closed January 29, 2026 and was accounted for as an equity transaction that reduced equity by $627 million (Q3 6-K chunk 8). On February 6, 2026 it closed the purchase of Telefónica's controlling 67.5 percent of Colombia Telecomunicaciones S.A. E.S.P. (Coltel) for about $214.4 million, of which $169 million was paid at acquisition (Q3 6-K chunk 9). Coltel was acquired with "Other debt and financing" of $1,424 million and lease liabilities of $515 million at fair value, and contributed revenue of $1,127 million and a net loss of $168 million from acquisition to September 30, 2026, including about $71 million of severance (Q3 6-K chunks 9-10). On April 27, 2026 it bought the remaining 32.5 percent from La Nación, a $219 million equity transaction (Q3 6-K chunk 9). The purchase accounting remains provisional. Creditor mechanic: control of the combined Colombian business is now full, which removes minority leakage and approvals but added acquired debt and integration costs; the management leverage rose to 2.76x at March 31, 2026 before falling to 2.53x at September 30, 2026 (CP-1). The Colombian joint operations (UNIRED and UT) are consolidated in full from the Coltel acquisition, and EPM remains a non-controlling partner in certain operations (Q3 6-K chunks 5, 22).

Ecuador and Uruguay. Millicom completed the purchase of Telefónica Móviles del Uruguay on October 7, 2025 for an enterprise value of $440 million and of Telefónica's Ecuador operations on October 30, 2025 for an enterprise value of $380 million (Q3 6-K chunks 13-14). Uruguay accounting is final; Ecuador's measurement period ended October 30, 2026 and was still being finalized when the statements were issued. Both carry local bank debt; a payment guaranty from MIC S.A. supports the Uruguay Santander loan (20-F chunk 256).

Chile with NJJ. On February 10, 2026 Celtel Chile, S.L. (49 percent Millicom, 51 percent NJJ Cactus SAS) bought Telefónica Móviles Chile for $50 million cash with contingent earn-outs "without recourse to Millicom"; Celtel carries a recognized liability of $110 million at September 30, 2026, funded by external financial debt, and mutual call options exist from the fifth and sixth anniversaries (Q3 6-K chunk 11). It is equity-accounted and the carrying value is nil because losses exceeded the investment, leaving $41 million of unrecognized losses at Millicom's share (Q3 6-K chunk 22). The 20-F describes the earn-out as up to $150 million (20-F chunk 297) and the 6-Ks as up to $490 million (see Conflicts). NJJ is described in the related party note as part of Xavier Niel's holdings (20-F chunk 295), so this is a joint investment with a party linked to the controlling shareholder; terms are as disclosed and the pricing basis of the options is not quantified.

Tower monetization and leaseback. On October 28, 2024 Millicom agreed to sell Lati International and other assets, more than 7,000 towers in Central America, to SBA Communications Corp. with a 15-year leaseback and a build-to-suit commitment for up to 2,500 further sites; Lati Paraguay was sold to Atis Group on June 3, 2025; the gain recognized in 2025 was $741 million (Q3 6-K chunks 14-15). Millicom retains Lati subsidiaries in Bolivia with about 2,000 towers (20-F chunk 91). Creditor mechanic (Analyst Interpretation): the sale converted owned assets into leased ones, so the leaseback added lease liabilities that rank as fixed claims; how the proceeds were applied is not stated in the sources reviewed.

Other portfolio actions. Tigo Paraguay signed on January 5, 2026 to sell its mobile finance business for a base price of $10 million with a potential $7 million earn-out (Q3 6-K chunk 12). The planned merger of Tigo Costa Rica with Liberty Latin America (agreement of August 1, 2024) was rejected by the regulator SUTEL in September and November 2025 (20-F chunk 83); the Costa Rica unit recorded a goodwill impairment of about $32 million in 2026, with goodwill of about $123 million remaining (Q3 6-K chunks 27-28). Tigo Sports local content was sold to FOX (agreement announced April 13, 2026; Q1 6-K chunk 22).

New debt issues and refinancings in 2026 (all subsequent to the 20-F balance sheet date). MIC S.A. reopened its 7.375% Senior Notes due 2032 for an additional $87.5 million in a Regulation S private placement on April 14, 2026, admitted to the Euro MTF market, placed with Banco General, S.A.; MIC S.A. issued an 8-year COP-USD linked private bond for COP 370,000 million at a fixed rate on March 27, 2026, subscribed by the Inter-American Development Bank and Proparco (Q3 6-K chunk 24). Tigo Paraguay redeemed its 5.875% notes due 2027, about $139.7 million, at par on April 29, 2026 (Q3 6-K chunk 25). Coltel entered a one-year $100 million bridge facility with Banco Santander at variable rate on April 13, 2026 to repay a $100 million HSBC facility, and later new three-year and one-year variable bank loans in Colombian pesos; Tigo Colombia added a four-year variable loan with Davivienda of COP 220,000 million; Tigo Panama refinanced a $75 million loan with a new six-year BAC loan in August 2026; Tigo Guatemala, Tigo Bolivia and others added bank loans (Q3 6-K chunks 23-25). After the quarter, Coltel took a COP 40,000 million BTG Pactual loan and prepaid $12.5 million of the Santander loan on October 15, 2026 (Q3 6-K chunk 28, subsequent event). Instrument-level terms such as ranking, security, covenants and guarantor groups are Not supplied for these issues, and use of proceeds is stated only for the Coltel bridge. Gross debt rose from $6,886 million to $8,648 million over the nine months (CP-1).

Capital returns. The AGM of May 20, 2026 approved a dividend of $3.00 per share in four quarterly installments and the Board on August 5, 2026 approved an interim dividend of $1.50 per share payable in January and April 2027 (Q3 6-K chunk 20). Share repurchases were $119 million in 2025 and none in the nine months of 2026 (20-F chunk 198; Q3 6-K chunk 5).

### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: service revenue of 6,045 for nine months 2026 against 3,888, with organic service revenue growth of 5.3 percent (Q3 6-K chunk 41), most of the growth coming from consolidating Coltel, Ecuador and Uruguay. Mechanism: recurring subscription revenue across twelve countries gives scale, and prepaid-to-postpaid migration raises visibility, but the acquired revenue base has a short history under Millicom control and the underlying organic rate is mid-single-digit. Implication: revenue is large and recurring; the comparison to prior years is flattered by perimeter, so organic growth is the better guide to durability. Conflict that counters it: none logged.

2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Adjusted EBITDA margin of 45.9 percent for nine months 2026 against 47.3 percent, with 149 of one-off items above Adjusted EBITDA (Q3 6-K chunks 34, 41). Mechanism: Coltel integration and restructuring are depressing near-term margin and consuming cash, while lease payments and spectrum are fixed claims. Implication: coverage and free cash flow depend on delivering the Colombian cost program; if integration slips, equity free cash flow guidance is at risk (management claim). Conflict that counters it: C3 does not change cash flow; the unreconciled operating cash flow figures in CP-1 gap G5 limit precision.

3. Concentration risk. Evidence: Guatemala and the two Colombian segments carry the largest segment revenue and the Guatemala entity issues $900 million 5.125% notes with subsidiary guarantees. Mechanism: a regulatory, currency or macro event in one of these countries affects a large share of consolidated EBITDA and the operating-level debt serviced from it. Implication: monitor country-level cash availability and the share of debt at operating entities (about 70 percent, Q3 6-K chunk 32), noting that MIC S.A. is dependent on upstream dividends (20-F chunk 111).

4. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: controlling shareholder holds about 42.2 percent, appoints four of eight non-executive directors, and has a related-party payable and a joint investment. Mechanism: aligned equity ownership can support the issuer, but larger distributions (a $1.50 interim on top of the regular dividend) and a related investment competing for cash with creditors are potential leakage channels. Implication: neutral to mixed on documented actions; the absence of documented creditor-adverse actions is not evidence that covenants prevent them because indentures are not supplied. Conflict that counters it: C2.

5. Key uncertainties. Evidence: Coltel and Ecuador purchase accounting provisional; covenant terms, debt schedule and revolving facility status not supplied; Chile earn-out size in conflict (C1); Guatemala litigation settled but other claims remain. Mechanism: each limits the ability to size liquidity and covenant headroom. Implication: committee readiness is limited until the named documents are obtained.
### Consumers
| Module | Readiness | What it should take from CP-1A | Why it matters | Gap and required action |

| CP-2 | Ready with limitations | Business model, concentration, ownership and control facts, transaction history, behaviour assessment and the three logged conflicts | Frames business risk and sponsor alignment for the credit view without new evidence | Missing indentures, covenant terms and rating information; carry Insufficient Information rows as gaps, not adverse findings |

| CP-5 | Ready with limitations | Every row's source, locator and category; conflicts C1 to C3 | Allows trace of claims to quotes and detection of cross-module differences | Verify the 42.2 versus 44.1 percent ownership bases and the Chile earn-out figures against their own locators; the payable to Iliad Holding Group is Not explained |
## Calculations

None new. All figures are quoted from the sources or are references to the accepted CP-1 handoff. No percentage or ratio was computed in this module; the shares of service revenue (60 percent Mobile and 38 percent fixed in 2025) and the ownership percentages are as printed in the 20-F.
## Gaps
| Id | Severity | Missing datapoint | Why it matters | Action |

| A1 | High | Indentures, credit agreements and guaranty documents (change-of-control, guarantor groups, restricted payment, covenant definitions) are not supplied; context states legal documents "none" | Legal capacity for distributions, asset transfers and priming cannot be assessed; behaviour is judged on actions only | Obtain the exhibits listed in 20-F chunks 123-127 |

| A2 | High | Nature, terms and 2026 balance of the payable to Iliad Holding Group (195 at December 31, 2025) | A related-party claim that is large relative to cash; could indicate shareholder funding or deferred distributions | Request the note G.5 update for September 30, 2026 |
| A3 | Medium | Pro forma Adjusted EBITDA and cash flow for Coltel, Ecuador and Uruguay | Needed to judge whether acquired assets support the debt used | Request a management bridge |

| A4 | Medium | Terms and size of Celtel Chile financing and earn-out (conflict C1); who funds a call option | The Chile entity is outside group debt but linked through options and a joint investment with a related party | Obtain the SPA summary and Celtel debt terms |
| A5 | Medium | Ratings and outlook as of the as-of date | Market access and cost of refinancing | Obtain current agency reports |
| A6 | Medium | Spectrum renewal costs for licenses expiring in 2026 and after | Cash call and operating risk in Guatemala, Paraguay and Colombia | Request a renewal calendar and expected fees |
| A7 | Low | Customer concentration, churn and segment EBITDA for Q3 discrete by country | Margin resilience analysis | Obtain the Financial and Operational Data file |
| A8 | Low | The 20-F states that there are no off-balance-sheet arrangements; no 6-K updates this | Completeness | None |
## Next module

Proceed to CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) using this fact pack, the three conflicts (C1 to C3), the behaviour assessment and the gaps A1 to A8, then CP-5 (evidence trace validation). The most valuable next evidence is the set of indentures and credit agreements, a September 30, 2026 debt and maturity schedule, covenant certificates, and explanations of the Iliad Holding Group payable and the Chile earn-outs.

spans.text: ## Request

Subject: Millicom International Cellular S.A. (issuer id tigo; "MIC S.A.", Luxembourg parent of the Tigo group). As-of date: 2026-11-05 (cutoff 2026-11-05). Module: CP-2, fundamental credit synthesis, pathway credit_snapshot, public case, creditor perspective.

Reader question: what is the fundamental credit view, and which strengths, weaknesses, findings and risks drive it? Decision drivers: business risk (from CP-1A), financial risk and liquidity (from CP-1 figures) and the gaps that limit both.

Method limits observed: the evidence is upstream only. This synthesis works from the accepted CP-0, CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs and quotes no source text; every figure is a figure carried in the CP-1 handoff (USD millions unless stated). It gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion; recovery prospects appear only as a mechanic. Every conclusion is tagged with one category: Documentary Fact (the cited upstream row or CP-1 figure states it), Management Language (management's characterisation carried by an upstream row, qualified and not adopted), Analyst Interpretation (this module's reading of the cited basis) or Insufficient Information (the basis is missing; the missing datapoint and why it matters are stated). Missing evidence is never an adverse conclusion. Upstream rows are referred to by area (for example "CP-1A ownership and governance row") because this Markdown handoff has no row identifiers.
## Sources
### Issuer sources behind the upstream handoffs
CP-2 did not read source text. The four issuer sources below underlie the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs it relies on; they are listed for provenance and are cited only through those handoffs.
| Source (exact name) | sha256 |
| 6-K_2026-05-12_dp246578_6k.htm.jsonl | e31fa18185d3ceef7ba9e0133efc952dd4f43ccbd999e9a5f5b5af04d8dbf712 |
Run context (settings only, not issuer evidence): context, sha256 5b145622a49a1e38ec7885504ac944230be02601fefa1d2f3fb7d83ded83c956.
### Supplied handoffs
| Module | sha256 | Status and use |

| CP-0 | 533a512a1f3bb7bc99ba007a510cec3fdee3aeab214040d4ea601266e7a3d9fd | Source readiness; assessed CP-2 as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. Inherited limits: covenant terms, instrument-level debt after December 31, 2025, revolving facility status, unreviewed Q1 and Q3 statements, restated and re-presented comparatives, provisional purchase accounting, perimeter break |

| CP-1 | fe7d99399cef5dd86595e652b06e9adc0c0e7978006654d0393d9f885e47b23a | Accepted financials and credit metrics; basis for every figure below. Inherited gaps G1 to G13, in particular covenant terms Not supplied (G1), no instrument table after December 31, 2025 (G2), revolving facility availability Not supplied (G3), management leverage not reproducible (G4) |

| CP-1A | 8596dd7e17ec172b37486bf546dcfb005f6c7a6bd1a2256b504f11f560848eb5 | Accepted business, transaction, ownership and behaviour fact pack; it judged CP-2 "Ready with limitations". Inherited gaps A1 to A8 and conflicts C1 (Chile earn-out size), C2 (control statements), C3 (revolving facility extension) |

Signals from CP-1A that restrict confidence: readiness judgment for CP-2 is "Ready with limitations", not ready without conditions; its highest-severity gaps are the missing indentures and credit agreements (A1) and the unexplained payable to the Iliad Holding Group (A2). While these remain, the assessment confidence is below High.
## Findings
### Credit view
The fundamental credit view is stated here in prose before any table. Category: Analyst Interpretation. Confidence: Medium.

Basis: CP-1 figures for gross debt 8,648, net debt 7,983, cash 848, management leverage 2.53x, lease liabilities 3,190, nine-month Adjusted EBITDA 2,958, nine-month equity free cash flow 867 and the maturity ladder; CP-1A business, concentration, ownership and transaction rows.

Rationale (evidence, mechanism, implication): Millicom is a large, scaled, recurring-revenue operator across twelve Latin American countries whose earnings base has stepped up sharply through the 2025 and 2026 acquisitions in Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay. The consolidated net debt increased from 5,357 at December 31, 2025 to 7,983 at September 30, 2026, and management leverage moved from 2.17x to a peak of 2.76x and then to 2.53x at September 30, 2026. The mechanism is that purchase payments, consolidated acquired debt and a heavier lease and dividend burden were absorbed by a much larger EBITDA and equity free cash flow base; deleveraging now depends on integrating Colombia and delivering the stated cash flow. The credit implication is a business with sound operating scale and improving cash generation but with high absolute leverage, material lease obligations outside the headline measure, a near-term maturity and refinancing agenda and an incomplete view of covenant headroom. The fundamental view is therefore that debt service capacity appears supported on the reported period, with the quality of that support limited by perimeter effects, definition risk and missing legal documents. The confidence is Medium rather than High because covenant terms, instrument-level debt after December 31, 2025, the revolving facility position and indentures are not in the evidence set.

Thesis (Category: Analyst Interpretation): a scaled Latin American telecom group with recurring cash flows and improving but still elevated leverage after a step-change in Colombian consolidation: debt service looks supported by reported earnings and equity free cash flow, while integration delivery, shareholder distributions, refinancing and unsupplied covenant terms determine how much headroom actually exists.
### Key findings

1. The credit story is a consolidation story. Nine-month 2026 revenue of 6,440 and Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958 compare with 4,150 and 1,964 a year earlier, but the release attributes most of the growth to perimeter and currency, with organic revenue growth of 4.4 percent and organic Adjusted EBITDA growth of 8.8 percent. Basis: CP-1 figures and the CP-1A volume-drivers and Colombia transaction rows. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures; the reading that organic growth is the better durability guide is Analyst Interpretation. Mechanism: acquired revenue lifts coverage but has a short record under Millicom control. Implication: durability should be judged on organic trends and on the Colombian integration outcome.

2. Leverage has improved for two consecutive quarters but is measured on a management basis that cannot be reproduced. Management leverage fell from 2.76x at March 31, 2026 to 2.73x and then 2.53x at September 30, 2026, against a year-end target of below 2.5x. Simple net debt over reported last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA is 2.14x and 2.99x when lease liabilities are added (CP-1 Calculation 3). Category: Documentary Fact for the reported ratio and Analyst Interpretation for the simple ratios. Mechanism: lease costs are subtracted in the management denominator and acquisitions are pro forma, neither bridge is supplied. Implication: use the lease-inclusive view alongside the headline ratio, and treat the 2.5x target as a management claim.

3. Debt service capacity is supported by cash generation but nearly all of it is claimed by fixed uses. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958 covers interest on bonds and bank financing of 472 about 6.3 times and covers that plus lease interest about 4.2 times (CP-1 Calculation 6); equity free cash flow of 867 was followed by dividends paid of 587, leaving about 280 against acquisition payments of 924. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation. Mechanism: lease payments, spectrum and taxes are the largest fixed claims ahead of equity free cash flow. Implication: cushion for unplanned shocks is thinner than the headline EBITDA suggests.

4. Liquidity relies on refinancing access. Cash of 848 equals debt due within one year of 872; the 2027 SEK note and the 600 revolving facility, which was undrawn at December 31, 2025 and due October 2027, mature within about fourteen months, and the facility's current availability is Not supplied. Category: Documentary Fact for balances and maturities, Insufficient Information for facility availability. Mechanism: local bank facilities have been rolled routinely in 2026 and bond market access was shown by the 2032 notes reopening, but a dislocation would hit the near-term ladder first. Implication: monitor facility status and the 2027 maturities.

5. Shareholder distributions are rising at the same time as leverage is being reduced. The Board approved an interim dividend of $1.50 per share in August 2026 on top of the regular $3.00 per share cycle; the controlling shareholder group holds about 42.2 percent of voting shares. Scheduled cash dividends of about 629 follow September 30, 2026 (CP-1 Calculation 7). Category: Documentary Fact for the declared amounts; Analyst Interpretation for the pressure on deleveraging. Mechanism: distributions compete with debt reduction for equity free cash flow. Implication: neutral to mixed behaviour on the evidence, because capacity limits in the debt documents are not supplied.

6. Control and related-party links are concentrated. One shareholder group holds de facto control and four of eight non-executive board seats; a payable to the Iliad Holding Group of 195 at December 31, 2025 has no stated nature, and the Chile investment is held with NJJ, a party linked to the controlling shareholder. Category: Documentary Fact; absence of documented creditor-adverse actions is not evidence of contractual protection. Implication: governance risk is moderated by alignment but cannot be sized without the indentures.

7. Data quality and definition risk limit precision. The December 31, 2025 balance sheet was restated, 2025 comparatives were re-presented, Coltel and Ecuador purchase accounting is provisional, Q1 and Q3 statements are unreviewed, the Chile earn-out is stated as up to $150 million in the 20-F and up to $490 million in the 6-Ks (conflict C1), and 9M operating cash flow differs by 9 between the cash flow statement and the release reconciliation. Category: Documentary Fact. Implication: carry both values and label bases; do not treat any single reconciled figure as settled.
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths.

- Scale and diversification. Category: Documentary Fact. Revenue streams are recurring and spread across twelve countries, with Mobile and Fixed services, and the largest segments are Guatemala and the two Colombian segments. Mechanism: geographic spread reduces the effect of any single market. Basis: CP-1A company and concentration rows and CP-1 revenue figures.

- Strong and growing cash generation. Category: Documentary Fact. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2,958, operating cash flow of 2,289 and equity free cash flow of 867, with management guidance of around 1.1 billion for 2026 (Management Language, qualified). Mechanism: cash generation funds interest, leases and capex and supports deleveraging.

- Improving leverage trajectory. Category: Documentary Fact. Management leverage 2.53x at September 30, 2026 compared with 2.73x and 2.76x in the prior two quarters; net debt was stable quarter over quarter at 7,983. Mechanism: higher EBITDA and EFCF are offsetting acquisition debt.

- Funding diversification. Category: Documentary Fact. Bonds, bank loans, development finance institution loans and local-currency issuance at both corporate and operating levels; about 70 percent of debt is at operating entities and 30 percent at the corporate level. Mechanism: reduces dependence on a single market; but structural subordination of corporate creditors to operating-level debt is also implied (Analyst Interpretation).

- Local-currency matching and hedging. Category: Documentary Fact. 61 percent of gross debt is in local currency or swapped, and the 2027 SEK note is swapped to dollars. Mechanism: aligns debt with revenue currencies.

- Transparent, frequent reporting and a no-breach statement. Category: Documentary Fact. Quarterly releases with reconciliations; the 20-F states no covenant breach at December 31, 2025 and none anticipated for twelve months. Limitation: that statement is not updated in the 2026 reports and thresholds are Not supplied (Insufficient Information).
Weaknesses.

- High absolute leverage and lease burden. Category: Documentary Fact. Net debt of 7,983 and lease liabilities of 3,190; lease-inclusive net financing obligations of 11,173 against reported last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 3,734 (Analyst Interpretation on the ratio). Mechanism: leases rank as fixed charges and the tower leaseback increased them.

- Emerging-market, correlated exposure and currency volatility. Category: Documentary Fact. The release cites rapid appreciation of the Colombian peso, Paraguayan guarani and Boliviano and a regime change in Bolivia. Mechanism: reported dollar results and local-currency debt values swing with exchange rates; reversal would reduce dollar EBITDA.

- Integration and execution risk in Colombia. Category: Documentary Fact for the restructuring charges and the Coltel net loss; Analyst Interpretation for the risk. Mechanism: severance and integration costs reduce EBITDA and cash flow and delay synergies.

- Floating-rate exposure and cost of debt. Category: Documentary Fact. Fixed-rate debt fell to 56 percent of debt and the average interest rate was 8.3 percent. Mechanism: higher rates pass through to interest expense; rate sensitivity is Not supplied (Insufficient Information).
- Near-term maturities and facility dependence. Category: Documentary Fact. Cash of 848 against debt due within one year of 872. Mechanism: refinancing needs are recurring.
- Controlling shareholder influence and distributions. Category: Documentary Fact. See key finding 5 and 6.

- Provisional accounting and limited legal visibility. Category: Insufficient Information. Covenant definitions, indentures, guarantor groups and the revolving facility position are not in the evidence set, so legal capacity for distributions, asset transfers and priming cannot be assessed.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Category |

| Colombian integration and cost program shortfall | Severance, integration costs and weaker-than-planned synergies reduce EBITDA and equity free cash flow; Coltel recorded a net loss since acquisition (CP-1A transaction row; CP-1 one-off items) | Slower deleveraging; leverage target of below 2.5x at risk; debt service cushion thinner | Material | Analyst Interpretation |

| Refinancing and liquidity concentration | Cash of 848 against debt due within one year of 872 and facilities maturing in 2027; revolving facility availability Not supplied | Dependence on bank and bond market access; potential need to use liquidity lines | Material | Analyst Interpretation |

| Distribution policy versus deleveraging | Regular dividends plus a 1.50 per share interim, about 629 scheduled after September 30, 2026 (CP-1 Calculation 7) | Reduces cash available for debt reduction; headroom depends on restricted payment terms that are Not supplied | Material | Analyst Interpretation |

| Currency, rates and Bolivia | Local-currency revenues with dollar reporting; 44 percent of debt floating (100 percent less 56 percent fixed); Bolivian regime change | Dollar EBITDA and debt service can move against each other; interest cost increases pass through | Material | Documentary Fact for exposures; Analyst Interpretation for effect |

| Lease and capex payable obligations outside gross debt | Lease liabilities 3,190 and capex payables 2,101 at September 30, 2026 (CP-1 gap G9); supplier finance 163 at December 31, 2025 | Fixed claims rank alongside financial debt in practice; headline leverage understates financial obligations | Material | Documentary Fact |

| Control concentration and related-party exposure | Controlling shareholder group, four board seats, payable to Iliad Holding Group of 195 and a joint investment with NJJ | Possible leakage or strategic decisions benefiting equity; contractual protection Not supplied | Material | Analyst Interpretation |

| Legal and tax exposures | Claims against the group 217 with 91 provided; tax exposure 378 with 60 provided; Guatemala settlement of 99 with 68 payable over seven years | Cash calls beyond provisions possible | Minor | Documentary Fact |

| Spectrum renewal timing | Licenses with 2026 expiries in Guatemala and Paraguay and expired Colombian permits under renewal | Renewal fees and operating risk; costs Not quantified | Minor | Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information on cost |

| Measurement and definition risk | Non-IFRS leverage, restated and provisional accounting, unreconciled small differences (CP-1 G5, G6, G7) | Headline metrics may move on restatement; reconciliations needed | Minor | Documentary Fact |
## Calculations

None new. All figures and the ratios referred to (simple net debt to last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of 2.14x, lease-inclusive 2.99x, interest coverage of 6.27x and 4.20x for nine months, scheduled dividends of about 629) are taken from the CP-1 handoff, Calculations 3, 6, 7 and 8, and are not recomputed here. The 44 percent floating share is 100 percent minus the printed 56 percent fixed share (CP-1 interpretation). The 11,173 lease-inclusive net financing figure is net debt 7,983 plus lease liabilities 3,190 as in CP-1 Calculation 3.
## Gaps
| Id | Severity | What the synthesis lacks | Why it matters | Affects | Action |

| S1 | High | Covenant thresholds, definitions, test dates and headroom (CP-1 G1); indentures and credit agreements (CP-1A A1); context states legal documents "none" | Debt service headroom, restricted payment capacity and change-of-control terms cannot be assessed; assessment confidence capped at Medium | Assessment, risks, thesis | Obtain the revolving credit agreement, indentures and compliance certificates |

| S2 | High | Instrument-level debt schedule after December 31, 2025 and revolving facility availability (CP-1 G2, G3; conflict C3) | Liquidity and refinancing risk cannot be sized beyond the aggregate ladder | Liquidity finding, refinancing risk | Obtain a September 30, 2026 debt and maturity schedule and facility status |

| S3 | High | Nature, terms and 2026 balance of the payable to the Iliad Holding Group (CP-1A A2) | A large related-party claim relative to cash; may indicate shareholder funding or deferred distributions | Control finding, sponsor alignment | Request the related-party note at September 30, 2026 |

| S4 | Medium | Management leverage bridge and pro forma Adjusted EBITDA for acquired businesses (CP-1 G4, G8; CP-1A A3) | Headline leverage cannot be reproduced; acquired asset support for debt unproven | Leverage finding | Request the management bridge |

| S5 | Medium | Celtel Chile financing and earn-out size (conflict C1; CP-1A A4) | Linked entity outside group debt but connected by options and a related joint investment | Control and contingent obligations | Obtain SPA summary and Celtel debt terms |
| S6 | Medium | Ratings and outlook as of the as-of date (CP-1 G12; CP-1A A5) | Market access and refinancing cost | Liquidity and refinancing | Obtain current agency actions |
| S7 | Medium | Cash and covenant effects of the Guatemala settlement and other legal exposures (CP-1 G11) | Cash calls outside Adjusted EBITDA | Cash flow quality | Request amounts and timing |

| S8 | Low | Interest rate sensitivity, swap detail, churn, customer concentration and spectrum renewal costs (CP-1 G12; CP-1A A6, A7) | Sensitivity analysis and margin resilience | Risk severity ratings | Obtain the Financial and Operational Data file |
## Next module

Proceed to CP-5 (evidence trace validator) to test that the assessment, findings and risks above trace to the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs. The evidence actions that would raise confidence above Medium are the indentures and credit agreements, the revolving facility and covenant documents, a September 30, 2026 debt and maturity schedule, current ratings and an explanation of the Iliad Holding Group payable.
